title: Enhancing mechanical, thermal, and flame-retardant properties of polyester/flax composites with magnesium and calcium hydroxide nanoparticles
authors: Boopathy Krishnasamy; Amuthakkannan Rajakannu; Pradeep Kumar Bammidi; Mayakannan Selvaraju
source_version: Published original, collection publication 29 May 2026; accepted 16 March 2026
source_material_form_TGA_raw: Each polyester/flax composite, four woven-fabric layers, hand lay-up followed by compression molding; source section 2.6 assays the prepared composites
TGA_specimen_preparation: Source section 2.6 assays 9–12 mg samples of the fabricated composites under nitrogen at 20 mL/min, 30–700 °C, 20 °C/min. Separate aliquot drying, cutting, grinding, pan and through-thickness sampling are unreported.
LOI_method: ASTM D2863; calibrated oxygen-index chamber, oxygen concentration gradually reduced until flame could no longer sustain; mean of three trials; instrument model unreported
LOI_specimen_preparation: Finished polyester/flax composite specimens, 100 × 10 × 3 mm, measured in the calibrated oxygen-index chamber. The methods call the later UL-94 specimens conditioned but give no separate LOI conditioning temperature or duration.
source_numeric_evidence_description: Original Table 3 numerical TG values cross-matched to explicitly sample-labelled measured LOI in original section 3.5. Table 5 also gives the exact control LOI and qualified treated thresholds. No coordinates or pixels extracted.
TG_locator: Table 3, Properties of thermal degradation; section 3.4; own method section 2.6
LOI_locator: Section 3.5 first paragraph naming S1/S4/S6/S10; Table 5 and conclusion separately checked; measured-LOI method section 2.7
conditions_locator: Sections 2.1–2.2 and Table 1, composite preparation; own sections 2.6–2.7 TG and LOI methods
source_location: Indexed original SciELO journal HTML and published author-uploaded main text: sections 2.1–2.7, 3.4–3.5, Table 1, Table 3, Table 5 and conclusions. Original Figure 7/8 pixels and complete PDF bytes unavailable.
washing_state: Initial cured and post-cured manufactured laminate; no durability washing or thermal ageing assigned
treatment_chemistry: Polyester resin with magnesium hydroxide (MH) or calcium hydroxide (CH) nanoparticles as assigned in Table 1; no additional textile finishing step
treatment_method: Bi-directional woven flax fabric and MH/CH nanoparticles of nominal average size 30 nm were acquired from Go Green Enterprises, Chennai, India. Polyester resin, hardener and accelerator were supplied by Kovai Cheenu Enterprises, Coimbatore, India. The nanoparticles were dispersed in styrene monomer by ultrasonication for 30 min followed by magnetic stirring for 30 min, then mixed with polyester resin and source-reported 2 wt.% cobalt accelerator plus 2 wt.% MEKP. Styrene quantity and the two curing-agent percentage denominators are unreported; Table 1 nominal polyester/flax/filler fractions already sum to 100% and are not renormalized. Four 300 × 300 mm woven flax plies were manually impregnated, stacked in a release-wax-coated mild-steel mold and held at 2 MPa at room temperature for 72 h. Panels were post-cured at 50 °C for 2 h. No durability wash or post-fire preparation is assigned.
source_Tonset_definition: Section 3.4 explicitly calls To the onset degradation temperature. No fixed mass-loss threshold or tangent algorithm is given; this is not assigned to T5/T10.
source_Tmax_definition: Section 3.4 states Tmax1 and Tmax2 are two DTG peaks, with greatest weight loss at Tmax2. Separate source-labelled chronological DTG peaks are retained.
source_residue_definition: Table 3 Char residual (%) at 600 °C; own TG residue, not cone residue.
limitations: The original tables and state-specific prose support three initial prepared textile-laminate pairs. Evidence is from indexed original journal HTML and the published author-uploaded text; complete PDF bytes and Figure 7/8 pixels are unavailable. No numerical values are derived from plotted coordinates. The source gives an own measured LOI method and mean of three trials, without dispersion. The separate mechanical-test count of five is not assigned to TG or LOI. TG aliquot preparation, pan and replicate count are unreported. Onset is the source-defined To without a specified mass-loss threshold or tangent algorithm. Table 1 nominal composition is preserved; styrene and curing-agent mass bases are not reconstructed. The source makes inaccurate broad group claims: S4 and S6 are called hybrid MH–CH specimens in the conclusion, although Table 1 and the exact LOI paragraph assign them solely to MH and CH, respectively. The same conclusion gives a >24.4% LOI threshold for S10, whereas the exact results paragraph gives 24.4%; S10 is excluded. Higher-level claims that all residues increase or that S4/S7/S10 are the respective largest residues are not fully consistent with the individual Table 3 entries. No cross-sample values are corrected from those claims. Several cone, burn-time, burning-rate and mechanical summary statements disagree with their tables or units; none of those measurements is used as TG or LOI. The other six treated samples lack exact recoverable numerical LOIs outside unavailable Figure 8 and remain excluded.
sample_state: S1; initial four-ply laminate; 0 wt% MH and 0 wt% CH
composition: Table 1: 55 wt% polyester, 45 wt% woven flax, 0 wt% MH, 0 wt% CH; additional styrene and curing-agent accounting unreported
pairing_evidence: Table 1 defines S1 as the prepared four-ply woven flax/polyester laminate; Table 3 supplies its own measured TG row and section 3.5 explicitly assigns LOI 20.4 to the same source specimen label. The unfilled S1 is a flax-reinforced laminate, not neat resin. No precursor or separate component TG substituted.
